previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of cardiovascular and vascular disease was admitted for recurrent chest pain that worsened during dialysis. She was found to have a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and underwent stent placement in the LAD and diagonal artery. Post-procedure, she developed severe abdominal pain, and imaging revealed portal venous gas indicating bowel necrosis, leading to an extended right colectomy and temporary abdominal closure. She later developed an anastomotic leak requiring a third surgery with ileostomy creation. Complications included ventricular tachycardia, wound breakdown, and intra-abdominal abscesses, managed with amiodarone, wound VAC, antibiotics, and nutritional support via feeding tube. She improved over six weeks, with stable cardiac status and healing wounds, and was discharged to extended care rehab with plans for ongoing wound and ostomy management.
